text:
alice: quick q — i'm about to apply a tf change that reshuffles two /20 subnet pools to free up space for a new k8s nodepool. doing a canary migration for one AZ first. want a quick sanity check on routing, nat eip allocations, and svc exposure. plan attached below.

ben: send the plan output pls, especially route table diffs. also are we touching any PrivateLink endpoints?

alice: plan snippet: ```
module "subnet_pool" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo//infra/subnets?ref=canary"
  old_subnet_ids = ["subnet-aaaa","subnet-bbbb"]
  new_prefixes = ["10.40.0.0/20","10.41.0.0/20"]
}
resource "aws_eip" "nat_canary" {
  count = var.canary ? 1 : 0
}
resource "aws_route_table_association" "canary_assoc" {
  subnet_id = aws_subnet.canary.id
  route_table_id = aws_route_table.egress.id
}
```

carlos: are any SGs referencing the old subnet by cidr_block? if so you'll need to update rules or we'll drop traffic unexpectedly. also double-check any ipam allocations.

emma: fwiw our k8s nodepools use hostNetwork for a few system daemons — updated subnet might change node local routes. test with a tainted node in the canary ASG first. to check connectivity run: `kubectl --context prod-canary exec -it pod/toolbox -- curl -sv http://169.254.169.254` to confirm metadata path still works behind NAT.

frank: downtime question — can we do this with zero-downtime? my suggested canary: 1) create new subnet, 2) attach route table and nat eip, 3) drain one node, move its ASG to new subnet (or create new node in new subnet), 4) smoke test, 5) change service annotation for externalLB if needed. if anything fails, roll back by switching ASG back.

alice: thanks. one more: PrivateLink svc in the analytics VPC references the old route table for the acceptance subnet. i'll update its endpoint config in the same PR. is that risky?

ben: small risk — PrivateLink endpoint uses ENIs in subnets; if we replace subnets ENIs will move. Make sure endpoint's subnet list includes the new subnet before removing the old. otherwise traffic will blackhole.

carlos: +1 on checking flow logs for dropped traffic after you apply. `aws ec2 get-flow-logs` isn't great, but we have kinesis logs for the VPC — check for DENY on the canary node ip ranges.

alice: noted. terraform plan will include endpoint update. here's the plan summary lines i care about: 
```
~ aws_subnet.old_subnet (destroy)
+ aws_subnet.new_subnet (create)
~ aws_eip.nat (replace)
~ aws_route_table_association.canary_assoc (update)
~ aws_vpc_endpoint.analytics_privatelink (update)
```

devops-bot: ci/status — tfplan for branches/canary-subnet passed (1 check failed: tfvalidate warnings). See https://ci.redwood/1234 for full plan output.

frank: tfvalidate warnings => what do they say?

devops-bot: warning: `aws_eip` without `depends_on` may be allocated out of band; recommended to declare explicit dependency on `aws_internet_gateway` if ordering matters.

ben: add `depends_on = [aws_internet_gateway.main]` to eip binding or better attach EIP to nat gateway resource directly. keeps ordering deterministic.

alice: good catch. i'll update PR. final ask: anyone want to pair on the canary apply tomorrow 9:30am PT? i'll run the apply and frank will monitor metrics.

emma: i can watch kube calico and node logs, +1 for 9:30.

carlos: i'll be on for quick rollback help.

alice: thanks all — i'll push the small tf change and ping the channel when ready. :thumbsup:
